title: Police watchdog probes death of man in Winnipeg Police custody
article: Manitoba's police watchdog is investigating the death in Winnipeg Police custody last week reportedly of a member of a prominent Winnipeg family of restauranteurs and owner of a poplar local pizza restaurant.

On Thursday, Winnipeg Police notified the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU) of a call for service involving a man on the road on Osborne Street who police said was being aggressive and acting erratically. Police said when officers arrived on scene at shortly after 7 p.m., the man was detained, handcuffed and subsequently collapsed. Winnipeg Fire and Paramedic Service members attended, and immediately administered CPR. The male was taken to St. Boniface Hospital were he was later pronounced dead.

The IIU has assumed responsibility for this investigation which is standard practice whenever the actions of a police officer contributes to a suspect's death. As this matter involves a fatality, a request for a civilian monitor will be made to the Manitoba Police Commission.

Reports Monday indicated that George Simeonidis Jr., the owner of Santa Lucia Pizza on Corydon Avenue, was the deceased man. The Simeonidis family relocated to Winnipeg in 1974 after starting their pizza business in Thompson and the operation expanded to become one of the city's most popular pizza restaurants with multiple locations in Winnipeg.
Simeonidis Jr. died Thursday, just 11 days shy of his 45th birthday.
Witnesses or other individuals who have information or video footage that may assist this investigation are asked to contact the IIU toll free at 1-844-667-6060.
